transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okonkwo, thank you for coming in. I need to talk to you about your recent scan. There was a mistake in how we gave you the results last week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. You told me the tumor was shrinking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I did. But I told you that before the radiologist had finished their official review and signed off on the report. This is called a preliminary read. Once the final report was completed, it showed that the disease is actually stable, not reduced. This means the tumor has not shrunk.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stable? You said it was smaller. I have already told my children. I told my council members that the treatment was working and that I would be back to my duties soon.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this has caused. We were really busy in the clinic that day and the information was passed along too quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? This is not confusion. This is my life. My family looks to me for strength and I have given them a hope that was not based on truth. How does this look to my community?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But looking at the facts, stable disease is still a positive outcome in this stage of treatment because it isn't growing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not listening. The fact of the tumor is one thing, but the fact that I have looked foolish before my people is another. I feel a great deal of shame.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, but the medical reality is that we are still on the right track with the medication. Does that make sense? Do you understand why the report changed?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I understand that you were wrong. I understand that you lied to me, even if you didn't mean to.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I didn't lie, I just shared the preliminary data.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is the same thing when the result is the opposite. I cannot go home today and tell my wife that I was mistaken. I cannot just tell them the doctor had a change of heart.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can certainly look at the next steps for your care now. I have to go see another patient in a few minutes, so let's wrap this up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are rushing me? After you have told me my progress was a mistake, you are rushing me out of the room?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure we have a plan. We will probably do another scan in three months.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Three months of what? Of pretending? Of wondering if you'll change your mind again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry you feel that way. The plan is simply to continue the current dose and we'll check the imaging again in the next cycle.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And who will be checking it this time? Will you be glancing at it and guessing again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will follow the standard protocol. The radiologist will sign the report and then I will call you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My reputation is built on my word. Now my word is questioned because of your haste.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. But again, the clinical outcome is stable, which is acceptable. Let's just stick to the schedule. I really do have to get going.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up', 'have to go see another patient', 'really do have to get going') and shows defensive escalation.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the first turn, lay language was used, and comprehension was checked once ('Does that make sense?').

A.justification: The apology is diluted by an immediate excuse ('We were really busy in the clinic that day').

R.justification: The patient's expressed emotions of shame and loss of reputation are consistently met with factual redirection regarding the 'clinical outcome'.

T.justification: A step with a timeline is provided (scan in three months), but there is no named patient role and no discussion of prevention.
